title: A seasonal phase learned from shallow M5.5+ earthquakes in 2000-2012 gave no clear positive transfer in 2013-2025
abstract: We tested whether annual earthquake timing learned in 2000-2012 continued in 2013-2025. We used 2,568 training events and 2,558 later events from USGS ComCat, with preferred M 5.5 or more, depth 0-40 km, and absolute latitude of at least 20 degrees. Southern phases moved by half a year. The later harmonic coefficient along the training phase was +1.25%. Its conditional 95% year bootstrap interval was -11.07% to +13.65%. A cell-year rotation test that kept local clustering gave one-sided p = 0.417. Whole-year rotations gave p = 0.429. None of the specified checks gave clear positive phase transfer. This result does not exclude local seasonal responses or identify a water-load mechanism. Short test records, mixed preferred magnitudes, catalog changes, and dependence across cell or year boundaries limit inference. The bundle contains code, original aggregate results, a figure, an independent numerical audit, source hashes and a retrieval script. Raw and record-level source data remain external.

display.caption: Annual coefficients along the training phase and later estimates for all specified checks. Intervals resample the 13 later years and condition on training phase. Blue bars are later years. Negative values do not establish an opposite-phase effect.

citations.reason: Published seasonal-load null result informed our question. We add a different phase-transfer benchmark with overlapping dates, not independent confirmation.
